description: Components a json-render spec may name in temper-desktop. Props are closed JSON Schema (draft 2020-12): a prop not listed is refused, so no spec can pass a colour, an icon, or markup — colour enters only as a role: a categorical role (cat-1…cat-8), a doc-type role, or a condition. `checks` declares what JSON Schema cannot say (a count within its total, keys among columns, edges naming nodes that exist, which children a component holds); both gates read them from this file. Chrome (reach, stance, authorship, the way out) is drawn by the app and is deliberately absent.

RegionState.description: The state of a read that is not present: arriving, empty, gave-up, or failed. The sentence is composed from `label` (the region's noun, e.g. "history"); do not word it yourself. Use when content is not available; render the content itself when it is.

label.description: The region's noun: history, connections, proposals.

detail.description: What was being read, or the reason given. Shown after the sentence.

BoundedList.description: A bounded list that says what it omits. `total` is every matching item, `shown` how many rows follow as children, `scope` what the total counts ("since you last engaged"). The omission sentence is composed; do not word it yourself. Children are the rows (e.g. ResourceRef). When `state` is not present, no rows render and the state is shown instead.

total.description: Every item the list stands for, not only those shown.

shown.description: How many rows follow as children. Never more than total.

scope.description: What total counts: "since you last engaged", "in this context".

label.description: The list's noun, used when it is not present: activity, sources.

more.description: Offer to show more, `step` at a time. Emits `more`; a view action, never a write.

ResourceRef.description: A link to a temper resource by id. The app resolves the title, doc type and home; `titleHint` shows only while resolving and never stands in for the resource. Use for every mention of a resource.

id.description: A resource UUID, or its decorated slug-<uuid> ref.

titleHint.description: Shown only while the reference resolves.

block.description: A block within the resource, by its heading-stable id.

Stack.description: Lays its children out in one direction. Gaps and alignment are named steps, never lengths.

wrap.description: Horizontal only: let children wrap to further lines.

Grid.description: Lays its children out in equal columns, narrowing to fewer when the view is narrow.

Heading.description: A heading, plain text. Level 1 titles a view; 2 and 3 divide it.

Text.description: A paragraph of plain text — no markup. `tone` steps it back: body, muted, subtle; `label` is the small uppercase eyebrow.

example.text: Three of the five chapters are drafted.

Tag.description: A short label, tinted by a categorical role or a condition.

tint.description: A categorical role (cat-1…cat-8) or a condition. Never a colour.

Stat.description: One figure with its label: a value, an optional unit, and an optional change with its direction.

value.description: The figure, as a number or already formatted.

tone.description: Whether the change is good, bad, or neither; the direction alone does not say.

Timeline.description: Dated items in order, with what they omit. `total` is every item the timeline stands for; `items` are those shown. The omission sentence is composed; do not word it yourself.

total.description: Every item the view stands for, not only those carried here.

scope.description: What total counts: "in this context", "since Monday".

label.description: The view's noun, used when it is not present and in its accessible name.

ref.description: A resource UUID, or its decorated slug-<uuid> ref.

tint.description: A categorical role (cat-1…cat-8) or a condition. Never a colour.

Table.description: Rows under typed columns, with what they omit. `total` is every row the table stands for; `rows` are those shown, each keyed by column. A `category` column tints its values through `tints` (value → cat-N); a `list` cell is a few short values. `page` says which rows of the total these are and whether more follow; `sort` names the order they are in; `facets` count the whole listing by a field, not only this page. The omission sentence is composed; do not word it yourself.

page.description: Show the page that starts at `offset`. A view action the host handles, never a write; without a host handler no pager is drawn.

sort.description: Order the rows by a sortable column. A view action the host handles, never a write; without a host handler no header is a control.

total.description: Every row the view stands for, not only those carried here.

scope.description: What total counts: "in this context", "since Monday".

label.description: The view's noun, used when it is not present and in its accessible name.

kind.description: How cells render: a resource cell is a resource id, drawn as a link; a category cell is tinted through `tints`; a list cell is a few short values.

additionalProperties.description: A categorical role, cat-1…cat-8. Plugins bind their vocabulary to these; never a colour.

sortable.description: Whatever answered the rows can order them by this column.

page.description: Which rows of the total these are: they start at `offset`, a page holds at most `size`, and `more` says whether rows follow this page, as the answer said.

sort.description: The column the rows are ordered by, and which way.

facets.description: Counts over the whole listing by one field each, not only the rows shown.

active.description: The value the listing is narrowed to, when it is.

unlisted.description: How many values are not listed in `counts`.

fieldsNotShown.description: Fields the rows carry that are not drawn as columns.

Chart.description: A line, bar, area or scatter chart. Each series takes a categorical role. `total` is every point the chart stands for; the points carried are those shown, and the omission sentence is composed.

total.description: Every point the view stands for, not only those carried here.

scope.description: What total counts: "in this context", "since Monday".

label.description: The view's noun, used when it is not present and in its accessible name.

kind.description: date: each x is an ISO 8601 date string.

tint.description: A categorical role, cat-1…cat-8. Plugins bind their vocabulary to these; never a colour.

Section.description: A titled part of a view. Inside Tabs it is one tab; inside Accordion, one collapsible item; anywhere else, a titled block.

Accordion.description: Collapsible Sections, one or many open at a time. Its children are Sections.

multiple.description: Let more than one Section be open at once.

Tabs.description: Sections shown one at a time, chosen by their titles. Its children are Sections; the first is shown first.

label.description: What the tabs choose between, for their accessible name.

Graph.description: Nodes and the edges between them, drawn read-only, with what it omits. `total` is every node the graph stands for; `nodes` are those shown. A node with no edge among those carried is listed beneath the drawing, not drawn. A node's `tint` is a doc-type role, a categorical role (cat-1…cat-8) or a condition, never a colour; a node with none is drawn neutral. `kind` is the word for what a node is (a doc type: "task", "character") and is shown beside its colour in the graph's legend, so colour never carries identity alone. A node may carry what the corpus knows of it: `corpusDegree` named beside the in-view degree, an `excerpt`, its `stage`, when it was last `updated`, and its `home` with `homeKind`. Edges join nodes by `id` and carry the relation's own terms — `edgeKind`, `polarity`, `label`, `weight` — the drawing grammar is derived from; edges between one pair share a line, and an edge joining a node to itself is stated beneath, not drawn. `arm` says where the view was read from: a walk from seeds within a depth, or an entry read anchored at nodes with a k. `bounds` is what an entry read says it drew. `cut` is what the catalog's bounds clipped off the answer, and a cut draws to the bounds. `ref` makes a node's listing a link to that resource. In a `radial` layout, `core` nodes settle at the centre. The omission sentence is composed; do not word it yourself.

nodes.label: Temper is worked from the desktop
nodes.excerpt: The goal every desktop slice advances.

nodes.label: Catalog: a read-only Graph
nodes.excerpt: Graph grows to the reads' own terms.

total.description: Every node the graph stands for, not only those carried here.

scope.description: What total counts: "around this goal", "the most-connected in this context".

label.description: The view's noun, used when it is not present and in its accessible name.

layout.description: force (the default) lets structure place nodes; radial settles `core` nodes at the centre and rings the rest.

arm.description: Where the view was read from: a walk from seeds within a depth, or an entry read anchored at nodes with the k applied.

from.description: The ids of the nodes the walk starts from, as drawn.

in.description: The ids of the anchor nodes the entry read was asked at, as drawn.

k.description: The draw limit the read applied.

bounds.description: What an entry read says it drew: `drawn` of `eligible`, `inScope` all told, and whether the read was truncated.

cut.description: What the catalog's bounds clipped off the answer: the nodes and the edges not drawn, each said only when some were. A cut draws to the bounds.

id.description: Unique within the graph; edges name nodes by it.

kind.description: What the node is, in a word: a doc type or a plugin's own term. Shown with the node.

tint.description: A doc-type role, a categorical role (cat-1…cat-8) or a condition. Never a colour. Omitted, the node is neutral.

ref.description: A resource id or decorated ref: the node's listing links to it.

core.description: Radial layout only: settle this node at the centre.

corpusDegree.description: The node's edge count across the whole visible corpus, named beside the graph's in-view degree.

excerpt.description: The resource's own first words, cut visibly before they arrived.

stage.description: Where the resource stands, in a word.

updated.description: When the resource was last touched: an ISO 8601 date or date-time.

home.description: Where the resource is homed: the anchor's words, or its bare id when unmatched.

label.description: The relation, shown as the edge's tooltip. A `derived_from` label draws as the derived role and dashes; a `contradicts` label draws in the danger role.

edgeKind.description: The relation's structural kind: contains solid, leads_to long-dashed, express dotted, near short-dashed and symmetric.

polarity.description: Which end carries the arrowhead: forward (the default) at target, inverse at source. A `near` relation heads neither end.

weight.description: How strong the relation is, drawn as the line's width. Absent, the line is drawn unweighted — a stated width, never a default weight.
